messages:
Aisha - Sales: Kicking off a POC for FinSaaS prospect. Requirement: EU + Canada only for customer data (multi-tenant app). Questions: can hosted API guarantee no egress to US for inference and logs, what's the current sub-processors list for EU/CA, how does BYO-KMS impact routing/pinning, and rough pricing delta for tenant pinning/geo-pin? Any known enterprise blockers?
Tom - Eng: Short answer: we can do regional data plane in europe-west1 and northamerica-northeast1. Control plane currently runs in US, so metadata/usage logs may go to US unless Private/VPC. Hosted + tenant pinning can keep inference in EU/CA but call out control-plane caveat.
Liam - Solutions: Pricing note: tenant pin + geo-pin typically adds overhead — ballpark +25–40% on per-token cost depending on model family and request concurrency. Dedicated reserved capacity changes the math. I'll pull example calc for their usage.
Marta - Security: A few clarifications: BYO-KMS — do they require keys to never leave customer region? Also need completed vendor security questionnaire and DPA/SCCs. If they require HSM-backed BYO with strict residency for key material, that pushes towards Private.
Natalie - EngInfra: Operational note: For strict "no-US egress" we recommend Private or Dedicated in a VPC. Hosted with regional inference reduces egress for payloads, but logs/metrics and control-plane metadata may still touch control-plane services in the US. If customer can tolerate metadata in US (no sensitive PHI), hosted is quicker.
Tom - Eng: Sub-processors quick list (high-level): GCP europe-west1 (data plane), GCP northamerica-northeast1 (Canada), monitoring vendor (EU nodes), CDN/edge provider, telemetry aggregator (US). I can generate a scoped subprocessor attestation for the POC.
Aisha - Sales: They also want to avoid automatic failover to outside EU/CA. Is that configurable?
Tom - Eng: Yes, we support routing policies. Options: strict geo-pin (reject requests outside allowed regions) or soft-fallback (route within allowed regions). Example config snippet:
```
routing_policy:
  mode: GEO_PIN
  allowed_regions: [europe-west1, northamerica-northeast1]
  failover: disabled
```
Aisha - Sales: Perfect, please put that in a one-liner I can send to legal/ops.
Liam - Solutions: One-liner for deck: "We can enforce geo-pinning to EU + Canada for inference; control-plane metadata may traverse US unless Private is selected. Geo-pin with no external failover increases availability risk and may affect SLAs."
OpsBot: Ticket created: #POC-3421 — infra provisioning for eu+ca geo-pin (ETA ~3 business days). Assigned: Natalie, Tom.
Marta - Security: Also flagging that legal will require DPA + SCCs (EU). If they insist on full control-plane residency, that elevates to Private deployment review — needs stakeholder sign-off and ~4–6 week lead time.
Aisha - Sales: Thanks. Can someone drop the subproc PDF and a short pricing blurb into the ticket so I can include in the customer's SOW?
Tom - Eng: Dropping public subproc page: https://redwood.ai/docs/subprocessors. I'll attach the scoped PDF to #POC-3421 and DM the detailed infra notes. Pricing blurb for SOW (short): "Geo-pin + tenant pin increases unit cost ~25–40% depending on token volume and model family; Dedicated commit pricing available on request."
Liam - Solutions: I'll add a slide with cost scenarios. :thumbsup:
Marta - Security: No blockers for POC start as long as customer signs vendor questionnaire and accepts control-plane caveat. If they require everything in-region including control-plane, mark POC as Private and start enterprise onboarding.
Aisha - Sales: Next steps captured: 1) send questionnaire to customer; 2) confirm BYO-KMS residency requirements; 3) get control-plane caveat sign-off or escalate to Private; 4) infra provisioning via #POC-3421; 5) share pricing scenarios. Thanks all.
